text:
Maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's scheduler tweak we saw a consistent p99 bump on the small-req cohort (seq_len <= 64). attaching profiler snapshot and a short log.
Raj: Got it. which tweak exactly? max_wait_ms or max_batch_tokens?
Maria: I lowered max_wait_ms from 12 -> 6 to reduce tail for long requests. config excerpt:\n```scheduler:{\n  max_batch_tokens: 8192,\n  max_wait_ms: 6,\n  microbatch_target: 16\n}```
Lee: Hmm. lowering max_wait should reduce latency but also reduce batching opportunities. Could increase p99 if kernel selection flips to an unfavourable path.
Sam: Do we have KV cache hit rates for that cohort? If cache miss -> cold KV path and fallback kernel could be slower.
Maria: Yes — cache hit rate dropped ~8% for seq_len<=64 after the change. Perf-bot posted a heatmap: https://intra/perf/2101234567/heatmap.png :eyes:
perf-bot: Automated snapshot: p50 9ms -> 8ms, p95 23ms -> 26ms, p99 48ms -> 72ms; KV hit rate small-req: 78% -> 70%; kernel-fallback-count +420
Raj: kernel-fallback-count rise is suspicious. Which kernel is being used now vs before?
Maria: Before: quantized-fused-attn (fast for short seqs). After: fallback to generic-matmul on ~30% of microbatches. trace: `select_kernel(query_len=32, kv_cached=false) -> generic-matmul`
Lee: That matches. Lower max_wait_ms means smaller batches; if microbatch size < quantized threshold we route to generic kernel.
Sam: Could be multiple factors: microbatch sizing (due to fewer queued tokens), plus KV cache miss increases per-token overhead, pushing selector into fallback heuristics.
Raj: Repro steps to validate? we should run controlled sweep: vary max_wait_ms [3,6,12,24] + max_batch_tokens [4096,8192,16384], measure p95/p99 and kernel-selection ratio.
Maria: I already ran a quick sweep on canary with synthetic traffic. Findings:\n- max_wait_ms=24: best p99 (50ms) but p95 worse for long seqs due to longer batching;\n- max_wait_ms=6: p95 slightly better overall but p99 for short seqs spikes;\n- raising max_batch_tokens to 16384 re-enabled fused-quant kernel for more microbatches even at low wait.
Lee: So it's a tradeoff: keep small wait to help latency for long requests but increase max_batch_tokens to avoid kernel fallback for short ones.
Sam: Also check microbatch_target. If target too small, runtime may prefer generic kernels. microbatch_target 16 might be below threshold for fused kernel.
Maria: Agree. Next experiment I'm running: {max_wait_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=16384, microbatch_target=32} for 2h ramp, will post results.
Raj: Also add a probe that logs `selected_kernel` and `kv_hit` per-request (sampling 1/1000) so we can correlate exact events for p99 spikes.
Maria: Done — sampling enabled on the canary. small sample already shows fused-quant selection goes from 64% -> 86% when max_batch_tokens=16384.
perf-bot: New canary run (08:12-10:12): p99 dropped from 72ms -> 54ms for short seqs; p95 stable. KV hit recovered to 76%.
Sam: Nice. Any regressions on throughput? throughput (tokens/s) slightly down (~3%) due to less aggressive batching when wait higher.
Lee: That is acceptable if latency SLO improves. We should codify best-effort policy: prefer kernel-stable config for short seqs by bumping max_batch_tokens, keep max_wait_ms modest to help long tails.
Raj: Also add a dynamic selector: if microbatch token distribution skewed to short requests, temporarily increase max_batch_tokens. File a follow-up RFC.
Maria: I'll draft RFC + include the profiler outputs and probe logs. For now, revert canary to best config: max_wait_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=16384, microbatch_target=32.
Sam: 👍 Also add a dashboard alert when kernel-fallback-count increases >2000/hr.
Maria: Added alert. Thanks all. Will post RFC link in this thread.
Raj: Thanks — great investigation. :clap:
Maria: RFC: https://go/repo/rfcs/362-queue-coalescing-kernel-stability (draft)
